title: Agent Evaluation & Observability
description: Study trajectory and outcome evaluation, deterministic harnesses and tool fakes, tracing decisions and tool spans, and regression suites and adversarial cases. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Trajectory and outcome evaluation
lessons.description: Define both outcome and action-level acceptance criteria.
lessons.conceptOverview: An outcome score measures task success, while a trajectory review checks intermediate actions, authorization and efficiency. Correct final text can hide harmful tool use or unnecessary external changes.
lessons.whyItMatters: Successful output does not excuse incorrect intermediate actions.

lessons.title: Deterministic harnesses and tool fakes
lessons.description: Replace the dependency with a fixed response and a separately scheduled integration check.
lessons.conceptOverview: A reproducible harness controls tool responses, clocks and initial state. Simulate errors and side effects rather than relying only on live services, and validate final state as well as returned messages.
lessons.whyItMatters: Controlled fixtures make orchestration failures reproducible.

lessons.title: Tracing decisions and tool spans
lessons.description: Design correlation IDs and span fields for a nested workflow.
lessons.conceptOverview: Trace each run with correlated tool calls, durations, versions and sanitized outcomes. Avoid retaining unnecessary secrets or personal data; diagnostic usefulness does not require logging every raw payload.
lessons.whyItMatters: Structured traces should connect failures to specific operations.

lessons.title: Regression suites and adversarial cases
lessons.description: Add a denied-action fixture and a bounded-termination assertion.
lessons.conceptOverview: Keep fixed tasks for ordinary success, denied actions, ambiguous requests and dependency failures. Compare changes on the same scenarios and inspect regressions by category instead of only average success.
lessons.whyItMatters: Evaluation must cover refusal boundaries and failure recovery.
